faq.a: Edibe is associated with the Arabic form أَدِيبَة, whose core sense is edibe; well-mannered, cultured (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Edibe?
faq.a: Edibe is associated with Arabic. Edibe is the Turkish form of Arabic أَدِيبَة (Adība), the feminine of أَدِيب, meaning 'well-mannered, cultured'.
Yes — the underlying form أَدِيبَة is Arabic.
Edibe can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Edibe should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Adība is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Edibe mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Edibe is rendered ادیبہ and carries the sense ادیبہ، باادب.

faq.q: What does Edibe mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Edibe is rendered ادیبه and carries the sense ادیبه، باادب.
A romanized syllable approximation is e-di-be. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Edibe?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Edibe, edibe. Script forms are أَدِيبَة, اديبه, ادیبه, ادیبہ, अदीबा.

faq.q: Is Edibe a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
